newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toshiba to go to market with DVD player in Nov.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba to go to market with DVD player in Nov.

text.p: Japan's Toshiba Corp said on Thursday that it would start selling its eagerly awaited digital video disc (DVD) player in Japan this November, aiming to become one of the first companies to come out with the next-generation recording system.
The electronics giant said it would start selling the DVD player at a price of 77,000 yen ($700) on November 1, the same day as rival Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd.
"Toshiba's new product launch is the company's first step to building a wide line-up of products and systems (for DVDs)," Toshiba said.
If all goes well, the company may start selling the electronic gadget in the United States by as early as the end of this year, it added.
DVD has large storage capacity and is expected to eventually make videocassette recorders, compact disc (CD) players and CD-ROMs obsolete.
The DVD system uses new laser technology to store up to 4.7 gigabytes of data on each side of a disc, enough to record 133 minutes of film and sound.

Toshiba said worldwide demand for DVD-related hardware is expected to reach 120 million units in calendar 2000. Together with software and applications, the DVD market has the potential to be worth billions of dollars.
Toshiba is one of 10 companies, mostly Japanese, which developed the DVD system.
Matsushita said in late August that it would launch two DVD models in Japan on November 1 at prices of 79,800 yen ($725) and 98,000 yen ($890).

Toshiba said Time Warner Inc is considering launching DVD software in the United States this year, and added that if the U.S. company does that, Toshiba will introduce its DVD player in the United States this year too.
The electronics giant also said it plans to start selling DVD players in other Asian countries in early 1997 and in Europe in the spring of 1997.

"As a leader in DVD, Toshiba is committed to promoting the development of a full range of products, and to the realisation of the technologies required for ultra-high-density, second- and third-generation DVD," Toshiba said.
Toshiba said it started sample shipments of the company's first DVD-read-only memory (ROM) drive for personal computer users on Thursday.
It will also start sample shipments of a DVD decoder board, which when coupled with a DVD-ROM enable computer users to watch movies on computer monitors, from the end of October.
"The company plans to follow up with large-screen TVs incorporating a DVD video player, and high-end desktop PCs featuring DVD-ROM drives," Toshiba said.
